design.title: The sponsorship desk
design.brief:
Yvonne, the COO, wants the sponsorship desk off spreadsheets. Here is how sponsorships work at Ulysses Tech Tips.

A SPONSOR is a company that pays to appear in videos. For each sponsor we keep a sponsor ID (unique), the company name, its industry, and one or more contact email addresses.

Some sponsors come to us through an AGENCY. An agency has an agency ID (unique), a name, and a commission rate. An agency represents many sponsors (or none yet); a sponsor is represented by at most one agency, and many sponsors deal with us directly with no agency at all.

Each VIDEO we publish has a video ID (unique), a title, a publish date, and a view count.

A sponsor buys slots in videos: a sponsor may appear in many videos or none, and a video may carry many sponsors or none. For each sponsor-in-video pairing we record the fee paid and the placement (pre-roll or mid-roll).
hints: 'One or more contact email addresses' is a multivalued attribute.
'At most one agency ... many with no agency at all' makes the AGENCY side optional.
Sponsor-in-video is M:N with attributes; those attributes belong on the relationship and end up in the bridge table.

relationships.name: Represents
relationships.rationale: A sponsor has at most one agency and often none; an agency represents many sponsors or none.

relationships.name: Sponsors
relationships.rationale: Many-to-many, optional both ways, with Fee and Placement on the relationship.

tables.name: SPONSOR_EMAIL
tables.note: The multivalued ContactEmail attribute becomes its own table.

tables.name: SPONSORSHIP
tables.note: The M:N Sponsors relationship becomes a bridge table holding Fee and Placement.

notes: SPONSOR.AgencyID must allow NULL. (The production database uses a surrogate SponsorshipID instead of the composite key; both are valid designs.)

design.title: The production floor
design.brief:
Ulysses Tech Tips needs a database for the people, the channels, and the products that make its videos.

Every EMPLOYEE has an employee ID (unique), a name, a job title, a hire date, and an annual salary. Each employee works in exactly one DEPARTMENT; a department has many employees or none yet. A department has a department ID (unique) and a name. Every employee except the founder reports to exactly one other employee, their manager; a manager may manage many employees.

The company runs several CHANNELS. A channel has a channel ID (unique), a name, a subscriber count, and a launch year.

Each VIDEO has a video ID (unique), a title, a publish date, a duration in minutes, and a view count. A video is published on exactly one channel, and a channel has many videos (a freshly launched channel may have none). Every video has exactly one employee as its host; an employee may host many videos or none.

The lab reviews PRODUCTS. A product has a product ID (unique), a name, a category, and a manufacturer's suggested retail price (MSRP). Each product is made by exactly one MANUFACTURER, which has a manufacturer ID (unique), a name, and a country; a manufacturer makes many products (or none we have reviewed yet).

A video may feature many products or none, and a product may be featured in many videos or none. For each product featured in a video we record the verdict given (recommended, mixed, or not recommended).
hints: 'Reports to exactly one other employee' is a unary 1:M relationship on EMPLOYEE; the founder makes the manager side optional.
Host and Works-in are two different 1:M relationships involving EMPLOYEE.
The M:N between VIDEO and PRODUCT carries the Verdict attribute.
In the schema, the unary relationship becomes a nullable ManagerID column referencing EMPLOYEE itself.

relationships.name: WorksIn
relationships.rationale: Each employee is in exactly one department; a department has many employees or none.

relationships.name: Manages
relationships.rationale: Unary 1:M: every employee has at most one manager (the founder has none); a manager has many reports or none.

relationships.name: PublishedOn
relationships.rationale: Each video is on exactly one channel; a channel has many videos or none.

relationships.name: Hosts
relationships.rationale: Each video has exactly one host; an employee hosts many videos or none.

relationships.name: Makes
relationships.rationale: Each product has exactly one manufacturer; a manufacturer makes many products or none.

relationships.name: Features
relationships.rationale: Many-to-many, optional both ways, with Verdict on the relationship.

tables.name: VIDEO_PRODUCT
tables.note: The M:N Features relationship needs a bridge table that carries Verdict.

notes: EMPLOYEE.ManagerID references EMPLOYEE and must allow NULL for the founder.

questions.text: List the name and subscriber count of every channel.
questions.sql: SELECT ChannelName, Subscribers FROM Channel

questions.text: List the name, title and annual salary of every employee.
questions.sql: SELECT EmpName, Title, AnnualSalary FROM Employee

questions.text: List the product name and MSRP of products in category '{{cat}}'.
questions.sql: SELECT ProductName, MSRP FROM Product WHERE Category = '{{cat}}'

questions.text: List the title and views of videos with more than {{v}} views.
questions.sql: SELECT Title, Views FROM Video WHERE Views > {{v}}

questions.text: List the name and hire date of employees in department {{d}} hired after {{y}}-12-31.
questions.sql: SELECT EmpName, HireDate FROM Employee WHERE DeptID = {{d}} AND HireDate > '{{y}}-12-31'

questions.text: List the distinct product categories, alphabetically.
questions.sql: SELECT DISTINCT Category FROM Product ORDER BY Category

questions.text: List every employee's name and salary, highest salary first.
questions.sql: SELECT EmpName, AnnualSalary FROM Employee ORDER BY AnnualSalary DESC

questions.text: List the distinct industries of our sponsors.
questions.sql: SELECT DISTINCT Industry FROM Sponsor

questions.text: List the titles of videos whose title contains the word '{{word}}'.
questions.sql: SELECT Title FROM Video WHERE Title LIKE '%{{word}}%'

questions.text: List the product name and MSRP of products priced between ${{lo}} and ${{hi}} inclusive.
questions.sql: SELECT ProductName, MSRP FROM Product WHERE MSRP BETWEEN {{lo}} AND {{hi}}

questions.text: List the manufacturer names based in either {{c1}} or {{c2}}.
questions.sql: SELECT ManufacturerName FROM Manufacturer WHERE Country IN ('{{c1}}', '{{c2}}')

questions.text: How many videos have we published in total? Return a single number.
questions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Video

questions.text: What is the total sponsorship revenue (sum of fees)? Return a single number.
questions.sql: SELECT SUM(Fee) FROM Sponsorship

questions.text: What are the longest and shortest video durations in minutes? Return both in one row.
questions.sql: SELECT MAX(DurationMin), MIN(DurationMin) FROM Video

questions.text: What is the average salary in department {{d}}, rounded to 2 decimals? Return a single number.
questions.sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(AnnualSalary), 2) FROM Employee WHERE DeptID = {{d}}

questions.text: For each channel ID, show the channel ID and the number of videos.
questions.sql: SELECT ChannelID, COUNT(*) FROM Video GROUP BY ChannelID

questions.text: For each video type, show the type and the average views, rounded to the nearest whole number.
questions.sql: SELECT VideoType, ROUND(AVG(Views)) FROM Video GROUP BY VideoType

questions.text: Show sponsorship revenue per placement: the placement and the sum of fees.
questions.sql: SELECT Placement, SUM(Fee) FROM Sponsorship GROUP BY Placement

questions.text: Show total views per publish month (YYYY-MM), in chronological order.
questions.sql: SELECT PublishMonth, SUM(Views) FROM Video GROUP BY PublishMonth ORDER BY PublishMonth

questions.text: Show the department IDs with more than {{n}} employees, with the count.
questions.sql: SELECT DeptID, COUNT(*) FROM Employee GROUP BY DeptID HAVING COUNT(*) > {{n}}

questions.text: Show the sponsor IDs that have paid more than ${{amt}} in total fees, with the total.
questions.sql: SELECT SponsorID, SUM(Fee) FROM Sponsorship GROUP BY SponsorID HAVING SUM(Fee) > {{amt}}

questions.text: List each employee's name together with their department name.
questions.sql: SELECT E.EmpName, D.DeptName FROM Employee E JOIN Department D ON E.DeptID = D.DeptID

questions.text: List each product's name with its manufacturer's name, for manufacturers from {{country}}.
questions.sql: SELECT P.ProductName, M.ManufacturerName FROM Product P JOIN Manufacturer M ON P.ManufacturerID = M.ManufacturerID WHERE M.Country = '{{country}}'

questions.text: List the title and views of every video on the channel named '{{ch}}'.
questions.sql: SELECT V.Title, V.Views FROM Video V JOIN Channel C ON V.ChannelID = C.ChannelID WHERE C.ChannelName = '{{ch}}'

questions.text: List each employee's name together with their manager's name (employees without a manager are excluded).
questions.sql: SELECT E.EmpName, M.EmpName FROM Employee E JOIN Employee M ON E.ManagerID = M.EmpID
hints: Join Employee to itself with two aliases: one for the employee, one for the manager.

questions.text: For each manager, show the manager's name and how many employees report directly to them.
questions.sql: SELECT M.EmpName, COUNT(*) FROM Employee E JOIN Employee M ON E.ManagerID = M.EmpID GROUP BY M.EmpID, M.EmpName

questions.text: For each host, show the host's name and the total views of the videos they hosted.
questions.sql: SELECT E.EmpName, SUM(V.Views) FROM Video V JOIN Employee E ON V.HostEmpID = E.EmpID GROUP BY E.EmpID, E.EmpName

questions.text: For each sponsor name, show the name and total fees paid.
questions.sql: SELECT S.SponsorName, SUM(SP.Fee) FROM Sponsorship SP JOIN Sponsor S ON SP.SponsorID = S.SponsorID GROUP BY S.SponsorName

questions.text: List the product name and verdict for every product featured in the video titled '{{title}}'.
questions.sql: SELECT P.ProductName, VP.Verdict FROM VideoProduct VP JOIN Product P ON VP.ProductID = P.ProductID JOIN Video V ON VP.VideoID = V.VideoID WHERE V.Title = '{{title}}'

title.from: SELECT V.Title FROM Video V JOIN VideoProduct VP ON V.VideoID = VP.VideoID GROUP BY V.VideoID

questions.text: For each manufacturer name, show the name and the number of times its products received the verdict '{{verdict}}'.
questions.sql: SELECT M.ManufacturerName, COUNT(*) FROM VideoProduct VP JOIN Product P ON VP.ProductID = P.ProductID JOIN Manufacturer M ON P.ManufacturerID = M.ManufacturerID WHERE VP.Verdict = '{{verdict}}' GROUP BY M.ManufacturerName

questions.text: For each channel name, show the name and the total sponsorship fees earned by its videos.
questions.sql: SELECT C.ChannelName, SUM(SP.Fee) FROM Sponsorship SP JOIN Video V ON SP.VideoID = V.VideoID JOIN Channel C ON V.ChannelID = C.ChannelID GROUP BY C.ChannelName

questions.text: For each video, show its title and its views per minute of duration, rounded to the nearest whole number.
questions.sql: SELECT Title, ROUND(Views * 1.0 / DurationMin) AS ViewsPerMinute FROM Video

questions.text: List the names of employees who earn more than the average salary.
questions.sql: SELECT EmpName FROM Employee WHERE AnnualSalary > (SELECT AVG(AnnualSalary) FROM Employee)

questions.text: List the names of products that have never been featured in a video.
questions.sql: SELECT ProductName FROM Product WHERE ProductID NOT IN (SELECT ProductID FROM VideoProduct)

questions.text: List the names of sponsors who sponsored at least one video on channel {{cid}}.
questions.sql: SELECT SponsorName FROM Sponsor WHERE SponsorID IN (SELECT SP.SponsorID FROM Sponsorship SP JOIN Video V ON SP.VideoID = V.VideoID WHERE V.ChannelID = {{cid}})

questions.text: List the title(s) of the most-viewed video(s).
questions.sql: SELECT Title FROM Video WHERE Views = (SELECT MAX(Views) FROM Video)

questions.text: List the names of employees who have never hosted a video.
questions.sql: SELECT EmpName FROM Employee E WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Video V WHERE V.HostEmpID = E.EmpID)

questions.text: Marketing wants one combined list of 'market segments': every sponsor industry and every product category, in one column, without duplicates.
questions.sql: SELECT Industry FROM Sponsor UNION SELECT Category FROM Product
hints: UNION stacks two SELECTs and removes duplicates.

questions.text: List every sponsor name with the number of sponsorships bought, including sponsors with zero.
questions.sql: SELECT S.SponsorName, COUNT(SP.SponsorshipID) FROM Sponsor S LEFT JOIN Sponsorship SP ON S.SponsorID = SP.SponsorID GROUP BY S.SponsorID, S.SponsorName

questions.text: List the name and title of the employee(s) who have no manager.
questions.sql: SELECT EmpName, Title FROM Employee WHERE ManagerID IS NULL

presentation.title: How many videos?
presentation.brief: Yvonne wants a single number on the wall: how many videos the company has published in total.
hints: A card with a count of VideoID.

presentation.title: Views by channel
presentation.brief: Which channel is pulling the most views? Show total views per channel name, largest first, with a title.
hints: Bars or columns; sort by value descending.
presentation.referenceSql: SELECT C.ChannelName, SUM(V.Views) FROM Video V JOIN Channel C ON V.ChannelID = C.ChannelID GROUP BY C.ChannelName ORDER BY 2 DESC

presentation.title: Sponsorship revenue over time
presentation.brief: The sponsorship desk wants to see total sponsorship fees per publish month of the sponsored videos, in chronological order, with a title.
hints: Fees live in Sponsorship; the month lives in Video. The model joins them for you.
Time on the axis: a line chart, sorted by the axis.
presentation.referenceSql: SELECT V.PublishMonth, SUM(S.Fee) FROM Sponsorship S JOIN Video V ON S.VideoID = V.VideoID GROUP BY V.PublishMonth ORDER BY 1

presentation.title: Verdicts by manufacturer
presentation.brief: The lab wants to know whether it is being too kind to any brand: for each manufacturer name, show how many products were featured, broken down by verdict. One visual, with a title.
hints: Manufacturer on the axis, Verdict as the legend, count of ProductID as the value.
Stacked or clustered columns both work.
presentation.referenceSql: SELECT M.ManufacturerName, VP.Verdict, COUNT(VP.ProductID) FROM VideoProduct VP JOIN Product P ON VP.ProductID = P.ProductID JOIN Manufacturer M ON P.ManufacturerID = M.ManufacturerID GROUP BY M.ManufacturerName, VP.Verdict ORDER BY 3 DESC

presentation.title: Payroll by department
presentation.brief: Finance needs exact figures: a table of each department name with its total annual salary, sorted from the biggest payroll to the smallest.
hints: Table visual; sum AnnualSalary; sort by the value.
presentation.referenceSql: SELECT D.DeptName, SUM(E.AnnualSalary) FROM Employee E JOIN Department D ON E.DeptID = D.DeptID GROUP BY D.DeptName ORDER BY 2 DESC

presentation.title: What works on the main channel?
presentation.brief: For the channel 'Ulysses Tech Tips' only, compare the average views per video type, highest first, with a title.
hints: Filter on ChannelName; use Average of Views, not Sum.
presentation.referenceSql: SELECT V.VideoType, AVG(V.Views) FROM Video V JOIN Channel C ON V.ChannelID = C.ChannelID WHERE C.ChannelName = 'Ulysses Tech Tips' GROUP BY V.VideoType ORDER BY 2 DESC
